sections.heading: What Is Low-E Glass and Why Does It Matter in Fairfax?
sections.body: Low-emissivity glass, commonly called Low-E glass, features an ultra-thin metallic oxide coating applied to one or more panes. This coating allows natural light to pass through while reflecting infrared heat — keeping interiors cooler in summer and warmer during Fairfax's cold winters. For commercial properties along Route 50 or residential communities near Mosaic District, this means greater occupant comfort and reduced strain on HVAC systems throughout the year. Low-E glass comes in several varieties, including hard-coat and soft-coat options, each suited to different performance needs and climate exposures. Fairfax experiences hot, humid summers and chilly winters, making thermal control a practical priority for any property owner. Our glazing professionals assess your building's orientation, existing window system, and usage patterns before recommending the right Low-E product for your specific situation. Upgrading to Low-E glass is one of the most impactful glazing decisions a property owner can make.

faq.q: How do I know if my windows need Low-E glass replacement?
faq.a: Common signs include visible condensation or fogging between glass panes, noticeable drafts near windows, rooms that are difficult to heat or cool, UV fading of furniture or flooring, and glass that is visibly cracked or broken. A professional glazing assessment can confirm whether your current glass units have failed seals or lack adequate low-emissivity coating.

faq.q: Can Low-E glass be installed in my existing window frames?
faq.a: In many cases, yes. If your existing frames are structurally sound, our glaziers can replace just the glass unit — removing the old pane and installing a new Low-E insulated glass unit cut to the correct dimensions. This approach is generally less costly and disruptive than full window replacement. We assess each situation individually to give you the best recommendation.
